title: Tom Brown's band and managing it, around 1912
summary: He became manager of Tom Brown's band, booking dances and fights at the Orleans Athletic Club.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: And there'd be a colored band, and then there'd be a white band, and maybe four more colored bands. All trying to out blast each other, see? So then we let, I last on with, with, with Red, Tom Brown. Mm-hmm. And we, playing around, playing here and playing there, playing the university, we played these, uh, I'd watch these, uh, social column, you know? Who's gonna give a dance, who's, who's getting engaged and all that. You know, I had nothing to do, so I didn't go to work in any place. Tom was a tinsmith.

Miller was a plumber. And, his brother Steve was, uh, he was a tinsmith too. And they all had jobs. I was the only guy that didn't have a job. So I, well, I got to find out, I got to be the manager of the band.
He told me that you used to get all the engagements and manage that he told us that, too.
That's right. So, and then, uh, we're playing, we're advertising the fights at the Orleans Athletic Club.
About how early can you remember any year that that was when you started with Tom Brown and Steve?
Yeah. So you were born, you say, 1889. 89. Yeah. So you were about 20, 23 years old.
